chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Sa'id al-Nisawi said: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughdi said in Marw that Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali said: Abd Allah ibn Asim said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays said, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman the Persian, in a long tradition which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to the city with one hundred Christians and what he asked Abu Bakr, but he did not answer him, then he was guided to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) and asked him some questions, and he answered him. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: Tell me, did you recognize Allah through Muhammad or did you recognize Muhammad through Allah, the Mighty and High?

Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) replied: I did not recognize Allah through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), but I recognized Muhammad through Allah, the Mighty and High, when He created him and established in him the boundaries of length and breadth. Hence I recognized that He was the Planner of the Produced through reasoning and inspiration from Him and will, just as He inspired the Angels to obey Him and made them know His self without similitude and without how. The tradition is long; we have taken from it the place of need, and I have transmitted it in its entirety at the end of the parts of the Book of Prophethood.

key_terms.بِلاَ شَبَهِ وَلاَ كَيْفٍ: Without similitude and without how (divine attributes)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) explain recognizing God through the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the theological depth of Imam Ali’s (AS) response to the Catholicos, emphasizing *tawhid* through the lens of creation (*khalaq*) rather than mere prophetic authority. By observing the Prophet’s physical attributes as signs of divine planning (*mudabbir*), Ali demonstrates that true knowledge of God is derived from recognizing the Creator’s will and inspiration, free from anthropomorphism (*tashbih*) or spatial description (*takif*). This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on rational deduction (*istidlal*) and divine inspiration (*ilhām*) as pathways to knowing the Essence of God.
